apis.name: BCryptGenRandom
apis.summary: Fills a buffer with cryptographically secure random bytes.
apis.description: BCryptGenRandom generates random data using either a CNG random-number algorithm provider or the system-preferred random number generator. When BCRYPT_USE_SYSTEM_PREFERRED_RNG is specified, hAlgorithm must be NULL and the system selects the generator. Otherwise hAlgorithm must be a handle to an RNG algorithm provider opened with BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider. The function writes the requested number of bytes and returns an NTSTATUS value; callers should test it with BCRYPT_SUCCESS or NT_SUCCESS rather than GetLastError.
apis.prototype: NTSTATUS BCryptGenRandom(BCRYPT_ALG_HANDLE hAlgorithm, PUCHAR pbBuffer, ULONG cbBuffer, ULONG dwFlags);

parameters.name: hAlgorithm
parameters.description: A handle to an RNG algorithm provider. This parameter must be NULL when BCRYPT_USE_SYSTEM_PREFERRED_RNG is set; otherwise it must be a provider handle opened for an RNG algorithm.

parameters.name: pbBuffer
parameters.description: A pointer to the buffer that receives the random bytes. The buffer must be at least cbBuffer bytes long.

parameters.name: cbBuffer
parameters.description: The number of random bytes to write to pbBuffer.

parameters.name: dwFlags
parameters.description: Flags that modify the operation. BCRYPT_USE_SYSTEM_PREFERRED_RNG selects the system-preferred generator and requires hAlgorithm to be NULL. BCRYPT_RNG_USE_ENTROPY_IN_BUFFER is also defined but is ignored on Windows 8 and later. Pass zero when using a provider handle.

return.success: STATUS_SUCCESS; the buffer contains cbBuffer random bytes.
return.failure: Another NTSTATUS value, such as STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER or STATUS_INVALID_HANDLE. Test with BCRYPT_SUCCESS or NT_SUCCESS; do not use GetLastError to interpret the result.

apis.remarks: The bytes are suitable for cryptographic use, but the call does not manage their confidentiality: callers should clear buffers that hold sensitive material when they are no longer needed. The system-preferred RNG avoids maintaining a provider handle and is convenient for one-off requests; BCRYPT_USE_SYSTEM_PREFERRED_RNG is not supported on Windows Vista without Service Pack 2. For key generation, use the key-generation interfaces appropriate to the algorithm rather than treating arbitrary random bytes as a ready-made key.
apis.maldev_notes: Cryptographic randomness is used for keys, nonces, initialization vectors, session identifiers, and randomized object names. It is ordinary in both benign and malicious software. In analysis, the relevant context is what the random data is used for, not the generation call by itself.
apis.defensive_notes: Random generation is ubiquitous in cryptography, networking, and application initialization. Large or repeated requests may be worth noting during cryptographic review, but randomness alone is not an indicator of malicious behavior.

apis.name: BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider
apis.summary: Opens a CNG algorithm provider and returns a handle for use with other BCrypt functions.
apis.description: BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider opens a cryptographic algorithm provider and returns a handle in phAlgorithm. The algorithm identifier selects the operation, for example BCRYPT_RNG_ALGORITHM for random generation, BCRYPT_SHA256_ALGORITHM for hashing, or BCRYPT_AES_ALGORITHM for symmetric encryption. The implementation parameter selects a specific provider or NULL for the default, and flags adjust provider behavior for the selected algorithm. The handle must be released with BCryptCloseAlgorithmProvider; it must not be passed to CloseHandle.
apis.prototype: NTSTATUS BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider(BCRYPT_ALG_HANDLE *phAlgorithm, LPCWSTR pszAlgId, LPCWSTR pszImplementation, ULONG dwFlags);

parameters.name: phAlgorithm
parameters.description: Receives a handle to the opened algorithm provider. On success, close it with BCryptCloseAlgorithmProvider when it is no longer needed.

parameters.name: pszAlgId
parameters.description: A null-terminated Unicode algorithm identifier, such as BCRYPT_RNG_ALGORITHM, BCRYPT_SHA256_ALGORITHM, or BCRYPT_AES_ALGORITHM. The identifiers are defined in bcrypt.h.

parameters.name: pszImplementation
parameters.description: The name of a specific algorithm implementation, or NULL to use the default provider for the algorithm.

parameters.name: dwFlags
parameters.description: Flags that modify provider behavior, such as BCRYPT_PROV_DISPATCH (kernel-mode only), BCRYPT_ALG_HANDLE_HMAC_FLAG, or BCRYPT_HASH_REUSABLE_FLAG. The applicable flags depend on the algorithm; pass zero for the default behavior.

return.success: STATUS_SUCCESS; phAlgorithm contains a valid provider handle.
return.failure: Another NTSTATUS value, such as STATUS_NOT_FOUND for an unknown algorithm or STATUS_INVALID_PARAMETER. Test with BCRYPT_SUCCESS or NT_SUCCESS.

apis.remarks: Provider handles have their own lifetime and must be closed with BCryptCloseAlgorithmProvider, including when they are used only for one operation. The algorithm identifier and flags determine which subsequent BCrypt operations are valid. Implementations are selected by name; passing NULL requests the default implementation.
apis.maldev_notes: CNG provider usage is standard for hashing, encryption, and random generation in modern Windows software. Security products and malware alike can use the same providers. The chosen algorithm and the operations that follow are more informative than the open call itself.
apis.defensive_notes: Provider and algorithm handles may appear in API telemetry. Unusual algorithm choices deserve context, but opening a provider is routine and is not proof of malicious intent.

example.title: Open an RNG provider, generate bytes, and close it
example.notes: The example demonstrates the provider lifetime: open, use, close. It checks each NTSTATUS value, clears the output buffer, and closes the provider on the normal path. It is illustrative only.

apis.name: BCryptCloseAlgorithmProvider
apis.summary: Closes a CNG algorithm provider handle.
apis.description: BCryptCloseAlgorithmProvider releases the resources associated with a provider handle returned by BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider. No flags are defined for dwFlags; pass zero. After a successful close the handle is no longer valid and must not be used with other BCrypt functions. The function returns an NTSTATUS value; callers should not assume that every close succeeds.
apis.prototype: NTSTATUS BCryptCloseAlgorithmProvider(BCRYPT_ALG_HANDLE hAlgorithm, ULONG dwFlags);

parameters.name: hAlgorithm
parameters.description: The provider handle to close. It must have been returned by BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider and must not already have been closed.

parameters.name: dwFlags
parameters.description: No flags are defined for this function. Pass zero.

return.success: STATUS_SUCCESS; the provider handle has been closed.
return.failure: Another NTSTATUS value, such as STATUS_INVALID_HANDLE if the handle is not valid. Test with BCRYPT_SUCCESS or NT_SUCCESS.

apis.remarks: Pass the exact handle returned by BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider and do not use CloseHandle for CNG provider handles. Closing a provider does not change the contents of buffers produced by earlier operations.
apis.maldev_notes: Closing a provider is a routine resource-management step in software that uses CNG. Its presence in analysis mainly helps establish the lifetime of cryptographic operations and is not a behavioral indicator.
apis.defensive_notes: Provider lifetimes can help correlate cryptographic activity, but ordinary applications open and close providers frequently. The close call is rarely distinctive on its own.

apis.name: CryptAcquireContextW
apis.summary: Acquires a handle to a cryptographic service provider and its key container.
apis.description: CryptAcquireContextW obtains an HCRYPTPROV handle for a CryptoAPI cryptographic service provider. The caller selects a provider type and may name a specific provider and key container. Flags control whether the function uses persistent keys, the machine key store, or a context without a key container. With CRYPT_VERIFYCONTEXT, the provider does not access persistent key storage, which is appropriate for hashing and random generation. The handle is released with CryptReleaseContext. Microsoft marks this API as deprecated and recommends CNG for new and existing software.
apis.prototype: BOOL CryptAcquireContextW(HCRYPTPROV *phProv, LPCWSTR szContainer, LPCWSTR szProvider, DWORD dwProvType, DWORD dwFlags);

parameters.name: phProv
parameters.description: Receives the provider handle on success. Release it with CryptReleaseContext when it is no longer needed.

parameters.name: szContainer
parameters.description: The name of the key container, or NULL to use the default container. When CRYPT_VERIFYCONTEXT is specified, this parameter must be NULL for file-based CSPs; hardware-based CSPs may permit a container name to access publicly available information.

parameters.name: szProvider
parameters.description: The name of the cryptographic service provider, or NULL to use the default provider for the requested provider type.

parameters.name: dwProvType
parameters.description: The provider type, which determines the supported algorithms. PROV_RSA_AES selects a provider supporting RSA and AES.

parameters.name: dwFlags
parameters.description: Flags that control the context. CRYPT_VERIFYCONTEXT requests a context without access to persistent key containers; CRYPT_MACHINE_KEYSET selects the machine key store, and CRYPT_NEWKEYSET or CRYPT_DELETEKEYSET manage containers.

return.success: A nonzero value; phProv contains a valid provider handle.
return.failure: Zero. Call GetLastError, which may return a CSP-specific NTE_* code such as NTE_BAD_KEYSET or NTE_KEYSET_NOT_DEF, or a standard error such as ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER.

apis.remarks: Microsoft marks this API as deprecated and recommends CNG (BCrypt) for new and existing software. Use CRYPT_VERIFYCONTEXT for operations that do not need persistent keys; use the key-container flags deliberately when managing persisted keys. The provider handle must be released with CryptReleaseContext, not CloseHandle. For private key operations that use a persisted container, the documented pattern is to try opening the container first and create it with CRYPT_NEWKEYSET if the call fails with NTE_BAD_KEYSET.
apis.maldev_notes: CryptoAPI contexts are used for hashing, encryption, and random generation in older and current software. Analysis may note the provider type, key container, and flags because they describe cryptographic configuration, but the call does not establish intent.
apis.defensive_notes: Persistent key containers can be relevant when investigating cryptographic state on a host. CRYPT_VERIFYCONTEXT indicates that no persistent container is being accessed, which is common for ephemeral hashing and random operations.

apis.name: CryptDecrypt
apis.summary: Decrypts data previously encrypted by using the CryptEncrypt function.
apis.description: Important This API is deprecated. New and existing software should start using Cryptography Next Generation APIs. Microsoft may remove this API in future releases. The CryptDecrypt function decrypts data previously encrypted by using the CryptEncrypt function. Important changes to support Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) email interoperability have been made to CryptoAPI that affect the handling of enveloped messages. For more information, see the Remarks section of CryptMsgOpenToEncode.

parameters.description: A handle to a hash object. If data is to be decrypted and hashed simultaneously, a handle to a hash object is passed in this parameter. The hash value is updated with the decrypted plaintext. This option is useful when simultaneously decrypting and verifying a signature. Before calling CryptDecrypt, the application must obtain a handle to the hash object by calling the CryptCreateHash function. After the decryption is complete, the hash value can be obtained by using the CryptGetHashParam function, it can also be signed by using the CryptSignHash function, or it can be used to verify a digital signature by using the CryptVerifySignature function. If no hash is to be done, this parameter must be zero.

The Final parameter must be set to TRUE only on the last call to CryptDecrypt, so that the decryption engine can properly finish the decryption process. The following extra actions are performed when Final is TRUE: If the key is a block cipher key, the data is padded to a multiple of the block size of the cipher. To find the block size of a cipher, use CryptGetKeyParam to get the KP_BLOCKLEN value of the key. If the cipher is operating in a chaining mode, the next CryptDecrypt operation resets the cipher's feedback register to the KP_IV value of the key. If the cipher is a stream cipher, the next CryptDecrypt call resets the cipher to its initial state. There is no way to set the cipher's feedback register to the KP_IV value of the key without setting the Final parameter to TRUE. If this is necessary, as in the case where you do not want to add an additional padding block or change the size of each block, you can simulate this by creating a duplicate of the original key by using the CryptDuplicateKey function, and passing the duplicate key to the CryptDecrypt function. apis.summary: Releases the handle of a cryptographic service provider (CSP) and a key container.
apis.description: Important This API is deprecated. New and existing software should start using Cryptography Next Generation APIs. Microsoft may remove this API in future releases. The CryptReleaseContext function releases the handle of a cryptographic service provider (CSP) and a key container. At each call to this function, the reference count on the CSP is reduced by one. When the reference count reaches zero, the context is fully released and it can no longer be used by any function in the application. An application calls this function after finishing the use of the CSP. After this function is called, the released CSP handle is no longer valid.
